SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ACTIVE LISTENING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Active LISTENING helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ACTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Respond to simple instructions retell stories told by the teacher 3. How do you seek in and out of school. and other learners. clarification in a.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Active LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Respond to simple instructions retell stories told by the teacher 3. How do you seek in and out of school. and other learners. clarification in a. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Active LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Active LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Active LISTENING?
